nodes.description: Progressive AHF can enter a neurologic phase with mental confusion, irritability, tremor, ataxia, generalized convulsions, delirium, and coma.

evidence.snippet: Neurological involvement begins with mental confusion, marked ataxia, increased irritability and tremors that are followed by delirium, generalized convulsions and coma.

nodes.description: Marked ataxia occurs with mental-status change, irritability, tremor, delirium, generalized convulsions, and coma in the neurologic phase of AHF.

nodes.description: AHF affects hematopoiesis, producing bone-marrow hypoplasia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia that reduce circulating white-cell and platelet counts.

evidence.snippet: Argentine hemorrhagic fever (AHF) is a viral disease caused by Junin virus and characterized by hematologic and neurological involvement.

nodes.description: Transfusion of convalescent immune plasma in defined neutralizing-antibody doses is the established specific treatment for AHF when administered during the prodromal phase, within eight days of symptom onset; a late neurologic syndrome is reported in a minority of immune-plasma-treated survivors.

evidence.snippet: Present specific therapy involves the transfusion of immune plasma in defined doses of neutralizing antibodies during the prodromal phase of illness.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of immune plasma in treatment of Argentine haemorrhagic fever and association between treatment and a late neurological syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In a double-blind trial patients with Argentine haemorrhagic fever treated with immune plasma within 8 days of the onset of the disease had a much lower mortality than those given normal plasma.

nodes.description: Direct infection of primary human endothelial cells increases endothelial permeability and disrupts adherens junctions, a cellular correlate of the vascular dysfunction and fluid-distribution abnormalities seen in AHF.

evidence.snippet: direct JUNV infection of primary human ECs results in increased vascular permeability as measured by electric cell substrate impedance sensing and transwell permeability assays.

nodes.description: Rodent contact or contaminated rodent excreta exposure initiates AHF by introducing Junín virus from its Calomys reservoir into an incidental human host. ECTO has no Junín- or rodent-excreta-specific term, so the exposure is bound at the broader viral-exposure level.

evidence.snippet: Argentine hemorrhagic fever (AHF) is a rodent-borne illness caused by the arenavirus Junin that is endemic to the humid pampas of Argentina.

nodes.description: Junín virus uses the human transferrin receptor 1 apical domain for New World hemorrhagic-fever arenavirus entry, enabling infection of susceptible human cells after spillover.

evidence.reference_title: Receptor determinants of zoonotic transmission of New World hemorrhagic fever arenaviruses.
evidence.snippet: Transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) is a cellular receptor for the New World hemorrhagic fever arenaviruses Machupo (MACV), Junín (JUNV), and Guanarito (GTOV).
